evidence.excerpt: Thyroid function is routinely assessed through a panel of three to five serum markers. Clinical guidelines define five functional categories—overt hypothyroidism, subclinical hypothyroidism, euthyroid, subclinical hyperthyroidism, and overt hyperthyroidism—but borderline cases generate significant inter-clinician disagreement. We trained one-vs-one kernel SVMs with radial basis function kernels on 6,730 labelled thyroid panels collected between 2012 and 2017 at two endocrinology outpatient clinics. Multiclass probability calibration used Platt scaling extended to the one-vs-one scheme. Overall accuracy on a stratified test split of 1,346 samples reached 88.3%. The two subclinical categories were most often confused, with confusion concentrated in samples where TSH differed from the midpoint of the reference range by less than 0.8 mIU/L. A confidence threshold was set such that panels with posterior probability below 0.65 for any predicted class were flagged for clinical review; this threshold captured 94% of misclassified cases at a flag rate of 21%.
